newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares end mixed, OTE telecom still depressed.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares end mixed, OTE telecom still depressed.

text.p: Greek shares were mixed at Thursday's close, finding it hard to build on earlier enthusiasm for banks, sparked by news of improving profitability in bellwhether National Bank.

On Wednesday, a high-level National Bank official told Reuters that first-quarter pretax profit had jumped 80 percent to 19.7 billion drachmas, boosted by increased income from traditional banking activities and gains from portfolio transactions.

"Today's results leak by National may be an indication of the willingness on the side of the market's institutional segment to support its blue chip core," said Vasilis Kaloudis, fund manager at International mutual funds.
Trading was active in blue chip banks and OTE and market-participants said investors were switching away from blue chips, seeking other profitable opportunities.
"But there is an increasing tendency for a switch away from banks and industrial blue chips which have led this year's rally and appear to have limited upside potential," said Kaloudis.
Investor interest is shifting towards medium-caps with good earnings growth prospects, placing emphasis on careful stock picking and relying less on sentiment, he added.
"Despite support from National Bank and other lead underwriters of the issue, there is continuing pressure in OTE largely from foreign portfolios," he said.
The market was seen in need of a new push from the macroeconomic front.
"The market suffers from a lack in fresh positive news on the macroeconomy as there are lingering fears on a rigid consumer price inflation and a widening trade deficit," Kaloudis said.

On Thursday, provisional Bank of Greece figures for February 1997 showed a widening in Greece's trade balance and current account deficit, coupled with a drop in May forex reserves after a brief attack on the drachma.
"We may well see the benchmark index drop below 1,500 points unless the market is given fresh impetus," Kaloudis said.
The Athens general index ended a net 0.11 percent or 1.67 points firmer at 1,543.25 from Wednesday's close of 1,541.58, having oscillated between 1,536 and 1,559 points.
Industrials bucked the trend with a 0.26 percent drop and banks were up 0.11 percent. Other sub-indices closed higher.
Turnover was moderate at 17.7 billion drachmas on volume of 4.5 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 128 to 86 with 31 shares unchanged on 245 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $12.25-$12.30. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,197-1,257 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998.
Shares of the underlying instrument closed down 15 drachmas at 6,600.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 528.42-562.14 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.05-$71.75. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,166-3,382 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.23-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 212-243 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
--Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
